title: Adaptive session economics PRD scratch
body:
Quick context
- Personal scratchpad for an experiment/rough PRD: "Adaptive session economics". Idea is to let apps define per-session economic constraints and have the runtime adjust fidelity, batching, model routing, and cache policy dynamically to meet them.
- Motivation: customers want predictable cost per conversation (or per session), but also want latency/quality guardrails. Current levers (static quantization, fixed model choice, manual batching configs) are brittle.

Problem statement
- SaaS apps see wildly variable token costs and latency across sessions (long LLM chats + high-fidelity models).
- Product teams either overprovision (expensive) or risk quality regressions when downgrading model globally.
- No simple per-user or per-session contract to say: "I will pay up to $X per session / preserve 95% of baseline quality / keep 200ms p50 latency".

High-level proposal
- Introduce a lightweight session-level contract (SessionBudget) that apps attach to session creation. SessionBudget expresses: max_cost (USD or token-equivalent), target_latency_ms (p50/p95), min_quality_score (relative/absolute), and preferred-skip-list (models/features not allowed).
- Runtime features to satisfy contract (adaptive engine):
  - Fidelity annealing: progressively reduce sampling temperature, model size, or output length limits when budget pressure detected.
  - Dynamic model routing: route to cheaper model variants (quantized, distilled) for non-critical turns; escalate to higher-fidelity model when triggers detect quality-sensitive turns.
  - Smart batching + prefetch: bias batching windows for sessions with relaxed latency targets; pre-warm KV cache for sessions with high TTL.
  - Micro-billing telemetry: attribute per-token cost and compute time back to session budget in near real-time to make decisions.

User stories (rough)
- As a frontend engineer, I want to create a session with a budget so that my product knows when to gracefully reduce features rather than crash my cost plan.
- As a platform engineer, I want signal in the Console to see which sessions are consuming disproportionately across customers so we can set alerts.
- As an ML eng, I want a hook to mark "critical" turns (function calling, synth outputs) that should never be downgraded even if the session hits budget pressure.

API sketch (session creation)
- POST /v1/sessions
  body: { user_id, session_name, SessionBudget: { currency: "USD", max_cost: 0.25, window: "per-session", target_p50_ms: 250, min_quality: 0.92, allowed_model_tiers: ["gpt-x-large", "open-distil"], critical_markers: ["function_call"] } }
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/budget -> returns live spend, remaining_budget, estimated_session_completion_probability
- Webhook: session_budget_exhausted (with suggestions: extend, degrade, close)

Runtime decision heuristics (notes)
- Maintain per-session scorecard: tokens_generated, compute_ms, model_tier_history, quality_estimate (via lightweight eval proxies or embeddings similarity to reference prompts).
- Cost burn rate estimator: running average of cost per token over last N turns, with upward smoothing for long responses.
- Escalation policy: if projected spend > max_cost, first try truncation + temperature reduction, then route to lower-tier model, finally block heavy features (long completions, plugins) and notify.
- De-escalation: if session sits idle or quality slack exists, restore fidelity gradually.

Observability and console UX
- Per-session card in Console: budget gauge, burn-rate chart, recent decisions (why we downgraded), and button to "commit extra budget".
- Alerts: notify dev when >1% of sessions for an org hit budget_exhausted in a 24h window.

Metrics and success criteria (initial experiment)
- Primary: mean cost per session for sessions with budgets vs control (target 20% lower with similar QA).
- Secondary: fraction of sessions that hit budget_exhausted (target <5%), p50 latency change, customer-reported quality delta (via small eval set).
- Operational: number of rollback incidents, false positive quality downgrades.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: internal alpha (SEs + solutions engineering) with feature flags and manual overrides.
- Phase 1: closed beta with 5 customers, billing sandbox (no real-dollar enforcement), Console visibility + webhooks.
- Phase 2: GA with optional enforced budgets and discounts for committed usage patterns.

Experiment ideas (quick)
- A/B model routing policy: always-route vs cost-aware routing for sessions with same budget - measure quality/latency/cost.
- Turn-level criticality tagging: let apps tag a set of turns as critical; measure whether fidelity annealing respects these markers and quality retention.
- Synthetic workloads: simulate chat patterns (e.g., 80% short Q/A, 20% long generation) to test burn estimator.

Compatibility and constraints
- Must work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (edge: private may have different cost semantics; budget should accept compute-units instead of USD).
- Backwards compatible: default session without SessionBudget should behave as today.
- Security: session budget metadata must be tenant-scoped.

Open questions / risks
- Quality measurement: cheap proxy vs full eval — cheap proxies may be noisy and lead to wrong downgrades.
- User experience: how noisy are the Console signals? Too many budget events could overwhelm devs.
- Billing model complexity: converting budget to policy decisions requires accurate pricing knowledge across model variants and regions.
- Edge case: multi-turn critical sequences where downgrading mid-sequence breaks context. Need safe-guards.

Next steps (for next week)
- Sync with infra: feasibility of per-session micro-metrics stream and fast budget decision path (low-latency). Action: schedule 30m with Priya + infra.
- Prototype of session card in Console (low-fi mock). Action: Mira to mock by Wed.
- Small spike: simulate burn-rate estimator on historical trace (ask analytics for 14 days of session logs). Action: Dylan to pull logs + run script.

Notes to self
- Keep the API minimal at first; complex knobs can be added later.
- Consider offering "economics presets" (startup, growth, enterprise) to make adoption easier.
- Document clear failure modes: when we "block features" we must surface deterministic fallback text to users.

Random brain fragments
- Could combine with "session presets" (persona/fidelity presets) — user picks preset then adds budget override.
- Think about pairing budget with rate-limit windows so apps can set burst budgets.

End of scratchpad.
